entities.summary: TrES-2b is an extrasolar planet orbiting the star GSC 03549-02811 located 750 light years away from the Solar System. The planet was identified in 2011 as the darkest known exoplanet, reflecting less than 1% of any light that hits it. Reflecting less light than charcoal, on the surface the planet is said to be pitch black, although it does emit dim red glow due to its temperature. The planet's mass and radius indicate that it is a gas giant with a bulk composition similar to that of Jupiter. Unlike Jupiter, but similar to many planets detected around other stars, TrES-2b is located very close to its star and belongs to the class of planets known as hot Jupiters.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The discovery of TrES-2b in 2011 provided significant insights into the properties and formation mechanisms of hot Jupiters, a class of planets that are increasingly being found around other stars. This finding has implications for our understanding of planetary formation and evolution.
